src.q: One Dostinex tablet contains 0.5 mg cabergoline.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Inhibition of physiological lactation soon after delivery, and suppression of established lactation (mother not breastfeeding for any reason, or after stillbirth or abortion).

src.q: Cabergoline is indicated for the inhibition of physiological lactation soon after delivery and for suppression of already established lactation

items.t: Hyperprolactinaemic disorders (amenorrhoea, oligomenorrhoea, anovulation, galactorrhoea), including prolactin-secreting pituitary adenomas, idiopathic hyperprolactinaemia and empty sella syndrome.

src.q: Cabergoline is indicated for the treatment of dysfunctions associated with hyperprolactinaemia, including amenorrhoea, oligomenorrhoea, anovulation and galactorrhoea.
Cabergoline is indicated in patients with prolactin-secreting pituitary adenomas (micro- and macroprolactinomas), idiopathic hyperprolactinaemia, or empty sella syndrome

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK SmPC or the MHRA pages accessed. MHRA fibrosis advice applies to chronic endocrine use, not to inhibition of lactation.

items.t: Inhibition of lactation: 1 mg (two 0.5 mg tablets) as a single dose on the first day after delivery.

src.q: For inhibition of lactation cabergoline should be administered during the first day post-partum. The recommended therapeutic dose is 1 mg (two 0.5 mg tablets) given as a single dose.

items.t: Suppression of established lactation: 0.25 mg every 12 hours for two days (1 mg total). Do not exceed a single dose of 0.25 mg in nursing women (postural hypotension).

src.q: For suppression of established lactation the recommended therapeutic dosage regimen is 0.25 mg (one-half 0.5 mg tablet) every 12 hours for two days (1 mg total dose).
A single dose of 0.25 mg of cabergoline should not be exceeded in nursing women treated for suppression of established lactation to avoid potential postural hypotension

items.t: Hyperprolactinaemia: start 0.5 mg per week in one or two doses; increase by 0.5 mg per week at monthly intervals to response. Usual dose 1 mg per week (range 0.25-2 mg per week). Maximum 3 mg per day. Split weekly doses above 1 mg.

src.q: The recommended initial dosage of cabergoline is 0.5 mg per week given in one or two (one-half of one 0.5 mg tablet) doses
The therapeutic dosage is usually 1 mg per week and ranges from 0.25 mg to 2 mg per week.
The maximum dose should not exceed 3mg per day.
Division of the weekly dose into multiple administrations is advised when doses higher than 1 mg per week are to be given

items.t: Valvulopathy is linked to cumulative dose: use the lowest effective dose and reassess benefit and risk at each visit.

src.q: Valvulopathy has been associated with cumulative doses, therefore, patients should be treated with the lowest effective dose.

items.t: Safety and efficacy not established under 16 years.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of cabergoline has not been established in subjects less than 16 years of age.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to cabergoline, excipients or any ergot alkaloid.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to cabergoline, any of the excipients listed in section 6.1 or any ergot alkaloid.

items.t: History of pulmonary, pericardial or retroperitoneal fibrotic disorders.

src.q: History of pulmonary, pericardial and retroperitoneal fibrotic disorders.

items.t: Hepatic insufficiency; toxaemia of pregnancy.

src.q: Cabergoline is contraindicated in patients with hepatic insufficiency and with toxaemia of pregnancy.

items.t: Do not give with antipsychotic medicines or to women with a history of puerperal psychosis.

src.q: Cabergoline should not be co-administered with anti-psychotic medications or administered to women with a history of puerperal psychosis.

items.t: Long-term treatment: evidence of cardiac valvulopathy on pre-treatment echocardiography.

src.q: For long-term treatment: Evidence of cardiac valvulopathy as determined by pre-treatment echocardiography.

items.t: Caution in severe cardiovascular disease, Raynaud's syndrome, renal insufficiency, peptic ulcer or GI bleeding, or a history of serious (especially psychotic) mental disorders. Particular care with other psychoactive medicines.

src.q: cabergoline should be given with caution to patients with severe cardiovascular disease, Raynaud's syndrome, renal insufficiency, peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, or with a history of serious, particularly psychotic, mental disorders
Particular care should be taken when patients are taking concomitant psychoactive medication.

items.t: Fibrosis and valvulopathy (pleural, pulmonary, pericardial, valvular, retroperitoneal) after prolonged use. Before long-term treatment: echocardiogram, ESR or other inflammatory markers, lung function/chest X-ray and renal function. Stop if echo shows new or worse valve regurgitation, restriction or leaflet thickening.

src.q: All patients must undergo a cardiovascular evaluation, including echocardiogram to assess the potential presence of asymptomatic valvular disease.
Cabergoline should be discontinued if an echocardiogram reveals new or worsened valvular regurgitation, valvular restriction or valve leaflet thickening

items.t: Symptomatic and postural hypotension can occur; take care with other blood-pressure-lowering medicines.

src.q: Symptomatic hypotension can occur with cabergoline administration for any indication.
Care should be exercised when administering cabergoline concomitantly with other drugs known to lower blood pressure.

items.t: Somnolence and sudden sleep onset: warn patients; those affected must not drive or operate machines; consider dose reduction or stopping.

src.q: Patients who have experienced somnolence and/or an episode of sudden sleep onset must refrain from driving or operating machines.

items.t: Impulse control disorders (gambling, hypersexuality, compulsive spending or eating): monitor regularly; consider dose reduction or tapered withdrawal.

src.q: Patients should be regularly monitored for the development of impulse control disorders.
Dose reduction/tapered discontinuation should be considered if such symptoms develop.

items.t: Lactation inhibition: avoid in pregnancy-induced (e.g. post-partum) hypertension unless benefit outweighs risk. Hypertension, MI, seizures, stroke and psychiatric disorders have been reported post-partum; monitor blood pressure and stop if hypertension, chest pain, severe headache or CNS toxicity occurs.

src.q: cabergoline should not be used in women with pregnancy-induced hypertension, for example, post-partum hypertension, unless the potential benefit is judged to outweigh the possible risk
cabergoline should be discontinued and the patient should be evaluated promptly

items.t: Hyperprolactinaemia: full pituitary evaluation before treatment. Fertility may return before menses; pregnancy test at least every 4 weeks while amenorrhoeic.

src.q: a complete evaluation of the pituitary is indicated before treatment with cabergoline is initiated
a pregnancy test is recommended at least every four weeks during the amenorrhoeic period

items.t: Contains lactose: not for hereditary galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Antipsychotic medicines: do not co-administer (section 4.3).

src.q: Cabergoline should not be co-administered with anti-psychotic medications

items.t: Dopamine antagonists (phenothiazines, butyrophenones, thioxanthenes, metoclopramide): should not be given together; may reduce the prolactin-lowering effect.

src.q: it should not be concurrently administered with drugs which have dopamine-antagonist activity (such as phenothiazines, butyrophenones, thioxanthenes, metoclopramide) since these might reduce the prolactin-lowering effect of cabergoline

items.t: Macrolide antibiotics (e.g. erythromycin): should not be used together; raise cabergoline exposure.

src.q: cabergoline should not be used with macrolide antibiotics (e.g. erythromycin) due to increased systemic bioavailability of cabergoline

items.t: Other ergot alkaloids during long-term treatment: not recommended.

src.q: the concomitant use of these medications during long-term treatment with cabergoline is not recommended

items.t: Other blood-pressure-lowering medicines: take care (hypotension).

src.q: Care should be exercised when administering cabergoline concomitantly with other drugs known to lower blood pressure.

items.t: Safety and efficacy not established in renal disease; give with caution in renal insufficiency. No numeric threshold given.

src.q: The safety and efficacy of cabergoline have not yet been established in patients with renal and hepatic disease.
cabergoline should be given with caution to patients with severe cardiovascular disease, Raynaud's syndrome, renal insufficiency

items.t: Section 4.3 contraindicates cabergoline in hepatic insufficiency. Section 4.4 separately advises considering lower doses in severe hepatic insufficiency (Child-Pugh C) on prolonged treatment (higher AUC).

src.q: Cabergoline is contraindicated in patients with hepatic insufficiency
Lower doses should be considered in patients with severe hepatic insufficiency who receive prolonged treatment with cabergoline.

items.t: Contraindicated in toxaemia of pregnancy. Otherwise use only if clearly indicated after benefit/risk assessment. Exclude pregnancy before starting; stop 1 month before planned conception; stop as soon as pregnancy is confirmed. Monitor pregnant women for pituitary enlargement.

src.q: Cabergoline should only be used during pregnancy if clearly indicated and after an accurate benefit/risk evaluation.
women planning to become pregnant should discontinue cabergoline one month before intended conception
If conception occurs during therapy, treatment should be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is confirmed to limit foetal exposure to the drug.

items.t: Cabergoline stops lactation: do not give to women with hyperprolactinaemia who wish to breastfeed. Advise not to breastfeed if lactation inhibition/suppression fails. Human milk excretion unknown.

src.q: Since it prevents lactation, cabergoline should not be administered to mothers with hyperprolactinemic disorders who wish to breast-feed their infants.
mothers should be advised not to breast-feed in case of failed lactation inhibition/suppression by cabergoline

items.t: Restores ovulation and fertility in hyperprolactinaemic hypogonadism. Women who want to avoid pregnancy should use mechanical contraception during treatment and after stopping until anovulation returns. After any treatment, prevent pregnancy for at least one month.

src.q: Cabergoline restores ovulation and fertility in women with hyperprolactinaemic hypogonadism.
Women who wish to avoid pregnancy should be advised to use mechanical contraception during treatment with cabergoline and after discontinuation of cabergoline until recurrence of anovulation.
after treatment pregnancy should be prevented for at least one month

items.t: Very common: valvulopathy and related disorders, headache, dizziness/vertigo, nausea, dyspepsia, gastritis, abdominal pain, asthenia, fatigue. Common: somnolence, depression, postural hypotension, hot flushes, constipation, vomiting, breast pain.

src.q: Cardiac disorders Very Common Valvulopathy (including regurgitation) and related disorders (pericarditis and pericardial effusion)
Nervous system disorders Very common Headache*, dizziness/vertigo* Common somnolence
Gastrointestinal disorders Very common Nausea*, dyspepsia, gastritis, abdominal pain* Common Constipation, vomiting**

items.t: Fibrotic reactions (pleural, pulmonary, pericardial, retroperitoneal) and cardiac valvulopathy: watch for breathlessness, persistent cough, chest pain, loin/flank pain, leg oedema or heart failure; investigate and stop if confirmed.

src.q: Pleuro-pulmonary disease such as dyspnoea, shortness of breath, persistent cough or chest pain.
cases of valvular and pericardial fibrosis have often manifested as cardiac failure

items.t: Post-partum use: hypertension, myocardial infarction, seizures, stroke or psychiatric disorders reported; stop and evaluate promptly.

src.q: Serious adverse events including hypertension, myocardial infarction, seizures, stroke or psychiatric disorders have been reported in postpartum women treated with cabergoline for inhibition of lactation.

items.t: Sudden sleep onset; impulse control disorders; psychotic disorder and hallucinations (frequency not known).

src.q: Not Known Aggression, delusions, hypersexuality, pathological gambling, psychotic disorder, hallucinations

items.t: Before long-term treatment: echocardiogram; ESR or other inflammatory markers; lung function/chest X-ray; renal function. Exclude pregnancy.

src.q: It is also appropriate to perform baseline investigations of erythrocyte sedimentation rate or other inflammatory markers, lung function/chest X-ray and renal function prior to initiation of therapy.
Before administration of cabergoline, pregnancy should be excluded.

items.t: First echocardiogram within 3-6 months of starting, then at least every 6-12 months. Serum prolactin monthly during titration.

src.q: the first echocardiogram must occur within 3-6 months
must occur at least every 6 to 12 months
Monitoring of serum prolactin levels at monthly intervals is advised

items.t: Post-partum: monitor blood pressure, especially in the first few days.

src.q: periodic monitoring of blood pressure, particularly during the first few days after cabergoline administration, is advised

items.t: Stop if echocardiogram shows new or worsened valve regurgitation, restriction or leaflet thickening; stop if pregnancy occurs.

src.q: Cabergoline should be discontinued if an echocardiogram reveals new or worsened valvular regurgitation, valvular restriction or valve leaflet thickening
Should pregnancy occur during treatment, cabergoline is to be discontinued.

items.t: MHRA: echocardiography within 3-6 months, then every 6-12 months; this fibrosis advice applies to chronic endocrine use, not to lactation inhibition.

src.q: echocardiography should be done within 3-6 months of starting treatment and subsequently at 6-12-month intervals
This new advice applies only to treatment of chronic endocrine disorders with these agents-it does not apply to the inhibition of lactation.

items.t: Oral; preferably take with meals (better tolerated).

src.q: it is recommended that cabergoline be preferably taken with meals for all the therapeutic indications

items.t: May cause drowsiness or sudden sleep; be careful driving in the first days; do not drive if sleepiness occurs.

src.q: During the first days of cabergoline administration, patients should be cautioned about re-engaging in activities requiring rapid and precise responses such as driving an automobile or operating machinery.

items.t: Tell the doctor about unusual urges (gambling, sex, spending, eating). MHRA: warn patients and carers and ask them to report unusual behaviour.

src.q: Healthcare professionals are advised to warn patients about these possible side-effects, and to inform patients to seek help from their doctor if they, their family, or their carer notice that their behaviour is unusual.

items.t: Report breathlessness, persistent cough, chest pain, loin pain or leg swelling.

src.q: Renal insufficiency or ureteral/abdominal vascular obstruction that may occur with pain in the loin/flank and lower limb oedema
